clause.text: Freedom to form and join a trade union.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the proscription orders infringed the petitioner's fundamental right to freedom to form and join a trade union under Article 14(1)(d).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed infringement of his fundamental rights under Article 14(1)(d) as the proscription prevented the J.V.P. members from organizing and functioning as a political group, analogous to a union of members.
case_context.respondent_argument: The Attorney-General argued that the President's immunity under Article 35(1) barred the proceedings and that the proscription was lawful under Emergency Regulations, not subject to challenge against the Attorney-General.
key_facts: The petitioner was a member of the J.V.P., a recognized political party.
The J.V.P. was proscribed by the President under Emergency Regulations.
The petitioner and members were prevented from functioning as a political party.
The petitioner alleged mala fide motives behind the proscription.
The petitioner cited infringement of Article 14(1)(d) rights.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court acknowledged the right to form and join associations under Article 14(1)(d) but held that the President's immunity under Article 35(1) prevented proceedings against the Attorney-General since the proscription was not under powers assigned under Article 44(2).
reasoning.application_to_facts: The proscription prevented the petitioner and others from organizing politically, but the court dismissed the petition on procedural grounds related to immunity and proper party.
principles_established: Absolute immunity of the President under Article 35(1) applies to acts not under Article 44(2).
Proceedings against the President for acts under Article 44(2) must be against the Attorney-General.
Proscription under Emergency Regulations is not an act under Article 44(2).

outcome.holding: The petition alleging infringement of Article 14(1)(d) rights was dismissed for lack of proper party and jurisdiction.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(d) was part of the petitioner's fundamental rights claim regarding the proscription's effect on political organization, but the court's immunity and procedural ruling prevented relief.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner claimed infringement of freedom to form and join a trade union under Article 14(1)(d) due to proscription; the court held the Attorney-General was not the proper respondent and dismissed the petition.
